heroHeadline: Day 591: Pemex CEO Replaced; Q1 Tourism Record (26.2M Visitors); USMCA Formal Round Confirmed for May 25; EU Summit on Track for May 22
heroSubtitle: On May 14–15, 2026 (Days 590–591), the Sheinbaum administration delivered two significant governance developments. The most consequential was the Pemex leadership transition announced May 14: Director General Víctor Rodríguez Padilla resigned per a prior 1.5-year agreement and was replaced by Juan Carlos Carpio Fragoso, the company's former CFO — the 15th cabinet change of the Sheinbaum presidency. Rodríguez Padilla's tenure produced a ~$23B USD debt reduction (down to ~$75B) and Mexico's first Pemex credit rating upgrade in over a decade. Carpio Fragoso inherits a financially stabilized company but faces ongoing production decline challenges. On May 15, Sheinbaum announced Q1 2026 tourism records: 26.2 million international visitors (+11.9% year-over-year in March) generating over $10.287B in revenues — historic figures ahead of the June 2026 FIFA World Cup opening at Estadio Banorte. The Social World Cup program will activate 4,000+ sports fields and launch an app with 290 tourist routes. On May 14, Sheinbaum also disclosed that the U.S. rejected 36 extradition requests from Mexico for insufficient evidence, and stated Mexico will apply the same evidentiary standard reciprocally — a notable sovereignty assertion in the ongoing Sinaloa Governor case. Diplomacy: The first formal USMCA bilateral negotiating round (week of May 25 in Mexico City) proceeds with Sheinbaum calling for insulation from U.S. midterm politics. The EU-Mexico Summit remains on track for May 22 when the modernized Global Agreement will be signed. U2's Bono joined Sheinbaum on May 14 at the Street Child World Cup assembly, calling her 'Mi presidenta.' Conagua also announced 11.97B pesos in Mexico City Metropolitan Area flood prevention infrastructure.
